content: {"summary":"Login 503 errors rose slowly in April 2025 because auth-db-01 kept presenting an expired TLS certificate despite a renewed file on disk; PostgreSQL did not reload the new certificate, causing TLS handshake failures for auth-service connections, and the connection‑pool retirement exposed the problem until the config was reloaded, after which 503s stopped.","likely_cause":"PostgreSQL on auth-db-01 failed to reload the renewed TLS certificate, so it continued presenting an expired cert, leading to x509‑expired handshake failures and a gradual increase in 503 login responses.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"auth-db-01 presented an expired certificate while the renewed file was on disk","evidence_ids":["INC-0031#1"],"quote":"what the server hands out carries a different serial from that file, and that certificate ran out at 09:00 today"},{"text":"PostgreSQL kept the previous certificate in memory and did not reload it after the file change","evidence_ids":["INC-0031#1"],"quote":"Postgres has kept the previous certificate in memory, and nothing has reloaded it since the files changed"},{"text":"The slow climb of 503s was caused by the connection pool retiring old connections that could not be replaced due to the expired cert","evidence_ids":["INC-0031#1"],"quote":"Our pool retires a connection after an hour, or after half an hour idle, both set in the `DATABASE_URL`"},{"text":"Reloading PostgreSQL configuration restored the renewed certificate and stopped the 503 errors","evidence_ids":["INC-0031#2"],"quote":"new connections succeed, the `503`s have stopped, logins look normal"}],"next_checks":["Verify that PostgreSQL automatically reloads TLS certificates after renewal","Add monitoring to compare presented certificate serial with the on‑disk file for auth-db hosts","Check that connection‑pool settings handle certificate reloads without service impact","Create an alert on x509‑expired handshake failures from auth-db"]}
